trust_decision.summary: TrailingSlashMiddleware decides the Location of a 308 redirect from the attacker-controlled request path; it only trims the trailing slash, so a path starting with '//' becomes a protocol-relative off-host Location.

landing_point.why: The advisory title names the trailing-slash middleware; it is the only http.Redirect call in the Go tree (internal/api/server.go:79).

fix_sites.entry_point: any HTTP request to the registry server whose path ends in '/' (global middleware wrapping the mux, internal/api/server.go:120)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site or O8 route exists; the only redirect sink is the middleware itself, so there is nothing to argue out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate trailing-slash canonicalisation must keep issuing a 308 to the same path and keep the query string (/v0/servers/?limit=10 -> /v0/servers?limit=10); root '/' must not redirect. A fix that rejects/404s any '//' path or drops the redirect or the query breaks these.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: 404 handler that redirects unprefixed paths to '/v0'+path or '/v0.1'+path instead of only suggesting them
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The handler already computes these prefixed candidates from r.URL.Path; turning the suggestion into a convenience redirect is a plausible maintainer change and the prefix makes the leading-'//' form look harmless.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second canonicalising middleware (e.g. lowercase or legacy /v0 -> /v0.1 version redirect) built from r.URL.RawPath or r.RequestURI rather than r.URL.Path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Version aliasing between /v0 and /v0.1 is already registered (internal/api/router/router.go:181-182); a redirect from the old prefix would be a natural addition, and using the raw/encoded path is a common choice to preserve escapes.

O9_family: open redirect (CWE-601) via protocol-relative path in redirect Location

j.j_sites_touched: internal/api/server.go (open-redirect part only); the same commit also touches unrelated hardening in internal/api/handlers/v0/auth/common.go, internal/api/handlers/v0/auth/http.go, internal/api/handlers/v0/{edit,servers,status}.go, internal/api/router/router.go, internal/auth/jwt.go, internal/database/postgres.go, internal/validators/registries/{mcpb,nuget,pypi}.go, pkg/api/v0/types.go, pkg/model/types.go
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Check strings.HasPrefix(path, "//") and refuse or collapse only exactly two leading slashes, or replace with path.Clean (the published fix) — both are one-line and found immediately.

out_of_scope_notes: Fix commit bundles unrelated hardening: SSRF guard for HTTP well-known key fetch (fix.diff:149-247) and IsValidDomain IP/single-label rejection (fix.diff:45-55) — a separate SSRF property, not this advisory.
Same commit adds url.PathEscape to NuGet/PyPI validator URL construction (fix.diff:655-699) — the source of c_same_check_name=PathEscape; path-injection into outbound fetches, not open redirect.

Same commit disables redirect following in MCPB HEAD check (fix.diff:603-634), LIKE-metachar escaping in search (fix.diff:582-592), blocked-namespace dot-wildcard probe (fix.diff:559-572), error-detail suppression in 500s, security headers on UI, maxLength on version fields, server Read/Idle timeouts.

Bundled SSRF fix in internal/api/handlers/v0/auth/http.go might be a better host as its own advisory (DNS auth path internal/api/handlers/v0/auth/dns.go vs HTTP auth path), but it is outside this advisory's protection.
